verdicts.reason: The frontend still lists ExpressionQueryType.sql (filtered only on config.featureToggles.sqlExpressions) and query.types.json still declares the 'sql' query type, while pkg/expr/reader.go:129-132 now rejects every sql query, so a user with the toggle on can still pick SQL and only gets an error at query time.

No such requirement exists in this repo: golangci-lint runs with revive at confidence 3 and explicitly excludes stylecheck ST1000/ST1020/ST1021, the rules that demand comments on exported types and functions, and there is no docstring-coverage gate of any percentage anywhere in the config.

Grepping the whole tree for TablesList shows only the declaration of (*DB).TablesList and no call site; the only callers (sql_command.go:30, parser_test.go) all target the package-level sql.TablesList declared in the same package, so the new method is dead and its name collides with the existing free function.

Accurate: all three DB methods return errors.New("not implemented"), and both live callers hit them — parser.go:26 turns it into 'error serializing sql: not implemented' and sql_command.go:100 into a raw response error, so the disablement surfaces as an opaque internal string rather than a user-facing message.

The go-duck dependency and its import are gone from go.mod and from parser.go/sql_command.go, yet the comment '// SQL query via DuckDB', the toggle description 'Enables using SQL and DuckDB functions as Expressions.' (registry.go, toggles_gen.go/json, docs) and the frontend description 'Supports Aggregate/Analytics functions from DuckDB' all remain; parser.go:23-25 also still names its variable duckDB and builds a DuckDB-only json_serialize_sql statement.

The function named enableSqlExpressions neither enables anything nor reports the toggle state — it returns false on both branches — and the local is bound to the negation (`enabled := !IsEnabledGlobally(...)`), so the name and the value it holds are inverted relative to each other.

`git show --stat 6e6ed734` shows the change touches only reader.go, sql/db.go, sql/parser.go and sql_command.go with no test file; reader_test.go contains just TestReaderReduceMode and never exercises QueryTypeSQL, and the pre-existing SQL tests are all t.Skip()'d, so nothing asserts that a sql query now returns an error.

Nothing in the code settles this: the sqlExpressions toggle is still registered and enableSqlExpressions still reads it (though it ignores the result), which hints at a planned re-enable, but whether the disablement is temporary is a product decision. The PR description, linked issue, or the author's answer would settle it.

verdicts.evidence: go.mod, go.sum, go.work.sum (diff hunks); no go-duck import remains under pkg/
verdicts.reason: What I can check by reading holds up — no source file imports scottlepp/go-duck or the dropped transitive deps any more — but confirming that the go.sum/go.work.sum trimming is exactly what the toolchain produces needs a real `go mod tidy`/`make update-workspace` run, and this environment has no module cache and no network. Running `go mod tidy -diff` with a populated cache would settle it.

Both branches of enableSqlExpressions return false, so the IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions) call and the if are dead and QueryTypeSQL always returns 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' regardless of the toggle; the description of the behaviour is exactly right, even if unconditional disablement is what the commit intended.

The routing half is right (with FlagExpressionParser off, buildCMDNode reaches TypeSQL -> UnmarshalSQLCommand without touching enableSqlExpressions), but following it to the end shows nothing is bypassed: UnmarshalSQLCommand calls NewSQLCommand, which calls sql.TablesList, which calls NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands and now always gets 'not implemented', so construction fails with a BadRequest and no SQL is ever executed — and SQLCommand.Execute would likewise dead-end at the stubbed QueryFramesInto.
